claims.text: Metal components used in hot-dip aluminum plating equipment are prone to degradation during contact with high-temperature molten aluminum.
BN can be applied to metal substrates by thermal spraying.
Thermal spraying produces a robust BN coating layer on the substrate.
The resulting BN coating is chemically inert toward molten aluminum.
The resulting BN coating is thermally stable under hot-dip aluminum plating conditions.
The BN coating prevents direct interaction between molten aluminum and the underlying metal substrate.
Preventing direct interaction with molten aluminum reduces chemical reactivity at the substrate.
The BN coating minimizes thermal stress in coated components.
Applying a BN coating significantly reduces corrosion and erosion by molten aluminum.
BN-coated components will undergo less corrosion and degradation than uncoated components under identical hot-dip aluminum plating conditions.
BN-coated components will retain structural integrity and functional performance for longer than uncoated components.
Applying a BN coating will extend the service life of hot-dip aluminum plating equipment.
The protective effect is expected at typical operational temperatures and immersion durations.
The magnitude of improvement and lifetime extension depends on coating thickness, application quality, and process parameters.
